seo.title: What is a web application?
seo.description: A web application is software that runs in a browser and does work, as opposed to a website that mainly publishes information.

definition: A web application is software that runs in a browser and does work, as opposed to a website that mainly publishes information.
answerBlock: A web application is software that runs in a browser and does work, as opposed to a website that mainly publishes information. Portals, dashboards, booking engines, quoting tools and internal systems are all web applications. They usually have accounts, permissions and data that changes constantly.

body.heading: What makes an application different from a website?
paragraphs: State and permissions. A brochure page looks the same to everyone; an application shows each person their own data and has to be certain who they are on every request. That means authentication, roles, audit trails and a server that never trusts what the browser sends.

It also changes how the work is planned. A marketing site is finished and then maintained; an application has a roadmap, releases and a support burden, and it should be budgeted that way from the start.

The technical shape follows: rendering that keeps the first view fast, a clear boundary between the interface and the business rules, and validation enforced on the server even where the interface has already checked it.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: Applications earn their keep by removing manual work: a portal that lets customers check their own orders removes the calls that ask about them.
They also raise switching costs in your favour, because a customer who runs part of their process in your system does not move casually.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Northmark Supply's quoting platform is an application rather than a catalogue: accounts, contract pricing and a quote that used to take three days now takes twelve minutes.

service.title: Web application development
service.line: Portals, dashboards, booking engines and internal tools built on Next.js with a typed API behind them.

terms.definition: An API is a defined way for two systems to exchange data without a person copying it between them.
